CASE 01 / PRIMARY · BFSI / FIELD OPERATIONS

Field Operation Platform

A mobile app for preparing visits, finding business details, and following up in the field.

Role
Product designer, from research to delivery
Scope
Field research, workflow architecture, interaction design
Worked with
Product, engineering, and field stakeholders
Key decision
Build around how agents work in the field, rather than copy the desktop product.

THE PROBLEM

The problem started before the first visit.

The brief was to design a mobile app. When I looked at an agent's day, I found that much of the work happened before and after the visit. Business details were spread across calls, notebooks, and desktop systems. I focused on bringing that information into the field workflow, so agents would not have to gather it again for every visit.

WHAT I DID

  • I followed agents through preparation, travel, visits, and follow-up to understand where they lost information.
  • I tried different ways to organise the workflow and checked them against what agents could do in the field.
  • I prioritised business lookup, qualification, and reliable lead capture instead of matching every desktop feature.

THE STRUCTURE

How I organised the mobile workflow

  1. 01PrepareReview the business before visiting
  2. 02VerifyCheck the details needed for the visit
  3. 03QualifyRecord lead details and next steps
  4. 04Follow upTrack visits and follow-up

THE RESULT

What the mobile workflow changed

The design brought preparation, business lookup, qualification, and follow-up into one app. Agents could review the business before a visit, capture leads in a consistent format, and record what needed to happen next.

Field workflow simplifiedPreparation, business lookup, lead capture, and follow-up in one mobile workflow.

CASE 02 / FIELD · LENDING / MARKET ENTRY

Kenya Lending Market Entry

A personal loan application designed for customers and lenders in Kenya.

Role
Lead designer, from application to onboarding
Scope
Market localisation, journey design, product pitch
Worked with
Product, engineering, and regional stakeholders
Key decision
Adapt identity checks, eligibility, and loan offers to the Kenyan market.

THE PROBLEM

Why the existing loan journey needed to change

The existing loan journey was not a direct fit for Kenya. I had to account for local customer behaviour, regulations, and the platform's technical limits when designing identity checks, eligibility, and loan offers.

WHAT I DID

  • I adapted the identity, eligibility, and offer steps for Kenya.
  • I considered local customer behaviour alongside what the existing platform could support.
  • I designed the full journey so product, engineering, and clients could review how it would work.

THE STRUCTURE

How I adapted the loan journey

  1. 01IdentityCustomer details and identity checks
  2. 02EligibilityChecks for the Kenyan market
  3. 03OfferClear lending decisions
  4. 04OnboardingA complete application flow

THE RESULT

From the pitch to client onboarding

The localised design helped clients see how the loan application would work for their customers. It supported the regional pitch and the team's first client onboarding in Kenya.

First clients onboardedThe team moved from the product pitch to onboarding its first Kenyan clients.

CASE 03 / FIELD · BFSI / DUE DILIGENCE

Due Diligence Platform (KYB)

A workspace for reviewing business details, checking risk, and recording KYB decisions.

Role
Sole product designer, from research to delivery
Scope
Research, information architecture, interaction design, delivery
Worked with
Product, engineering, and review roles
Key decision
Keep business evidence, review notes, and handoffs together so the next reviewer can follow the decision.

THE PROBLEM

Reviewers were rebuilding context by hand.

Reviewers had to gather business details from several screens before they could assess risk. They also needed to explain their decision and pass the review to someone else. I wanted the workspace to keep the evidence and the review notes together.

WHAT I DID

  • I mapped how each role found business evidence, reviewed it, and passed the work on.
  • I grouped related information, simplified labels, and designed ways to recover when a task could not be completed.
  • I checked whether the flow was understandable and feasible to build before finalising it.

THE STRUCTURE

How I organised the review workspace

  1. 01SearchFind the entity
  2. 02OrientSee business details and review status
  3. 03ReviewCheck evidence and risk flags
  4. 04HandoffPass on the evidence and review notes

THE RESULT

A clearer review and handoff

The design gave reviewers one place to read business details, inspect evidence, and record the next action. Clear grouping and a consistent handoff helped different roles discuss the same review.

Review workflow clarifiedReviewers could find business evidence and discuss risk without piecing the information together again.

This product is under NDA. I can discuss my role and approach without sharing confidential details.

CASE 04 / REGULATED · BFSI / IDENTITY

Video KYC for NBFCs & Banks

A video verification flow that helped customers complete identity checks while meeting compliance requirements.

Role
Product designer, research and delivery
Scope
Research, verification flow, recovery states, delivery
Worked with
Product, engineering, compliance, and operations
Key decision
Give customers clear instructions while keeping verification evidence visible to reviewers.

THE PROBLEM

What a video verification call needed to cover

Customers needed to understand what to do during a video verification call. Reviewers needed the required documents and a record they could audit. I designed the flow to support both sides of the call.

WHAT I DID

  • I mapped the call, document capture, and reviewer handoff.
  • I designed recovery steps for weak connections and incomplete documents.
  • I kept verification status visible and used clear instructions to help customers complete each step.

THE STRUCTURE

How I designed the verification steps

  1. 01PrepareReadiness and consent
  2. 02ConnectOne-to-one verification
  3. 03CaptureCompliant evidence
  4. 04ResolveReview and recovery

THE RESULT

A clearer call for customers and reviewers

The design made identity checks easier to follow while keeping the evidence, status, and review controls needed for compliance.

Clearer verification stepsLess friction during identity checks without compromising compliance.

I can walk you through the verification flow and how I handled interrupted calls.

CASE 05 / SYSTEM · BFSI / MONITORING OPS

Watchlist Monitoring

A risk monitoring prototype covering alerts, review tasks, permissions, and follow-up.

Role
Product designer, from requirements to prototype
Scope
Problem framing, interaction models, prototype, decision record
Worked with
Product and engineering validation
Key decision
Resolve system behaviour before polishing the interface.

THE PROBLEM

The brief described screens, but not the system.

The brief described a monitoring workspace but left several requirements open. I needed to work out how navigation, first use, permissions, and follow-up would behave before designing the final screens.

WHAT I DID

  • I reviewed the brief, identified conflicting requirements, and listed the questions the team needed to resolve.
  • I mapped the same tasks across permissions, empty states, severity levels, and error recovery.
  • I built alternative flows and recorded which choices still needed review from product and engineering.

THE STRUCTURE

How I organised alerts, reviews, and actions

  1. 01Signal intakeChanges enter one review queue
  2. 02TriageSeverity and status support scanning
  3. 03InvestigationKeep related evidence with the review
  4. 04ResolutionRecord actions and review history

THE RESULT

A prototype the team could review

The prototype let the team compare different flows instead of discussing requirements in isolation. I recorded what the design covered and which questions still needed product, engineering, or user input.

Decisions ready to validateA working prototype ready for validation.

I can show you the prototype and explain the decisions behind it.
